### When the Room Decides to Speak

The committee had gathered to debate a [compendium]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="compendium · n. 摘要,纲要"} of new communication guidelines. [Viz]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="viz · adv. 即；就是"}, no more [cant]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="cant · n. 斜面；伪善之言；黑话；角落; 倾斜；讲黑话; 把…棱角去掉；使…倾斜；甩掉; 行话的；哀诉声的；假仁…"}, no more [guff]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="guff · n. 〈美俚〉胡说,瞎扯,废话"}." Don't [mock]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="mock · vt. &amp; 愚弄；嘲弄; 使受挫折; 仿制的；模拟的"} the competition. Just [laud]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="laud · vt. 赞美；称赞; 赞美；称赞；颂歌"} what we actually built." A junior writer dropped a quiet [hint]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="hint · n. 暗示；线索; 暗示；示意; 示意"} that the whole opening was recycled [adage]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="adage · n. 谚语,格言"}s dressed up as insight — true enough that no one laughed.

Later, over coffee, the mood loosened into ordinary [chat]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="chat · vi. 聊天；闲谈; 与…搭讪；与…攀谈; 聊天；闲谈"}. ### The Morning Scoop

Before the editorial meeting, Dana sat down with her [diary]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="diary · n. 日记, 日记簿"} to [draft]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="draft · n. 汇票；草稿；选派；气流 起草；制定；征募 拟稿；绘样；作草图 初步画出或的；正在起草中的，草拟的；以…"} a quick [recap]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="recap · n. 翻新的轮胎; 翻新胎面；扼要重述"} of the week's stories. The big [scoop]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="scoop · n. 小铲；小勺; 一勺之量; 独家新闻; 用铲等挖; 抢先报道; 抢先获得，胜过"} — a whistleblower account she'd been nursing for days — was finally ready to go to [print]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="print · n. 印刷字体; 印成的图画, 图案, 版画; 照片; 印刷, 出版; &amp; 用印刷体写; 冲洗 P…"}. She had planned to write a measured [op-ed]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="op-ed abbr.专栏版，特写稿版"}, but her editor wanted a front-page splash instead. A [rumor]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="rumor · n. 谣言；传闻; 谣传；传说"} was already circulating online, and if they waited, a rival outlet would [blurt]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="blurt · vt. 突然说出, 脱口而出"} it out first.

She read her notes aloud, and the [irony]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="irony · n. 反语；反话; 具有讽刺意味的情况；出乎意料的情况；令人啼笑皆非的事情"} wasn't lost on her: a story about silence, told in the loudest possible voice. She used a [caret]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="caret · n. 脱字符号；插入符号"} to mark a missing clause, swapped a [comma]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="comma · n. 逗号；停顿"} for a dash, and paused to [parse]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="parse · v. 作语法分析；作句法分析; 对…进行语法分析; 语法分析，语法分析结果"} every sentence with the same care a linguist brings to an unfamiliar [lingo]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="lingo · n. 听不懂的话; 隐语;外语"}. One paragraph felt too self-congratulatory — she had wanted to [extol]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="extol · vt. 颂扬；赞美；赞颂"} the whistleblower's courage without sounding like a [bravo]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="bravo · n. 喝彩；亡命徒; 喝彩; 好极了 Bravo格兰德河, 布拉沃河, 大致向南流经新墨西哥州中部至得克萨…"}-hungry cheerleader. She cut the lines where she'd tried to [exalt]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="exalt · vt. 赞扬；歌颂; 提升，提拔"} her own reporting and tightened the [quote]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="quote · vt. 引述；举证；报价; 引用；引证；报价; 引用"} she'd pulled from the source.

Down the hall, the night editor was already [growl]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="growl · vi. 发狺狺声, 作隆隆声; 低声咆哮着说; 咆哮, 狺狺声"}ing at the layout team; someone had let a [smear]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="smear · vt. 弄脏；涂上；诽谤；把…擦模糊; 涂片；污点；诽谤; 被弄脏"} of ink ruin the proof. A junior reporter began to [bleat]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="bleat · vi. 叫, 咩咩的叫; 发出羊叫似的声音; 哭诉,抱怨; 胡扯; 轻声诉说; 咩咩地发出; 以颤抖可怜的声…"} about deadlines. The [noise]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="noise · n. 噪声，喧哗声; 声音；响声"} of the newsroom — keyboards, arguments, a [siren]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="siren · n. 汽笛, 警报器; 迷人的女人, 妖妇"} somewhere outside — pressed in from all sides. "[Hoots]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="hoots · int. 咄,啐"}," she shot back — her own borrowed interjection for *I couldn't care less about the hour either.*

She [liken]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="liken · vt. 把…比作；比拟"}ed the final edit to tuning an instrument: you [ditto]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="ditto · n. 同上；同上符号；很相似的人或物; 重复；照抄; 同上地; 相似的"} nothing, carry nothing forward unchanged. Every [query]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="query · n. 问题, 疑问; 质疑, 对…表示疑问"} gets answered, every rumor verified, every [smear]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="smear · vt. 弄脏；涂上；诽谤；把…擦模糊; 涂片；污点；诽谤; 被弄脏"} either proved or cut. She filed the piece at 4 a.m., silenced her phone, and let the presses do the rest.

### The Art of Getting Through to Someone

In the greenroom before a live panel, Mara and her co-host exchanged [banter]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="banter · n. 玩笑；逗乐; 开玩笑；说笑；逗乐; 取笑，逗弄"} that kept the nerves at bay — teasing each other about last week's [typos]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="typos · n. 打字稿"} in the show notes, laughing at every [cackle]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="cackle · n. 饶舌；咯咯声；闲谈; 咯咯叫；喋喋不休；饶舌; 格格笑著表示；喋喋不休地说"} that slipped out when a joke landed wrong. She'd once written a [spoof]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="spoof · n. 滑稽模仿; 玩笑，讽刺性文章; 滑稽地模仿; 发送电邮；发送仿真电邮；电邮欺骗; 哄骗；捉弄"} of the network's style guide, and the crew still quoted it. Such was the [byword]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="byword · n. 谚语，俗语；格言；笑柄"} of their partnership: if you can't laugh at the craft, you've already lost the audience.

The moment the red light blinked on, the tone shifted. Mara would [assert]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="assert · vt. 断言；主张；声称；维护，坚持"} her thesis with quiet conviction, never resorting to the [clamor]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="clamor · n. 喧哗声，喧闹; 大声的要求或抗议; 喧哗；吵闹; 大声地要求或抗议"} of talking heads who mistake volume for authority. When her guest [alluded]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="allude · vi. 提及, 暗指"} to a controversial study, she did not let the [cliche]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="cliche · n. 陈词滥调；铅版；陈腐思想; 陈腐的"} "the research is clear" slide past unchallenged; she chose to [debunk]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="debunk · vt. 揭穿真相, 暴露"} the misreading point by point, drawing on a broad [corpus]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="corpus · n. 文集；本金；语料库"} of peer-reviewed work to support her case. Her producer could [vouch]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="vouch · vt. 担保；证明；传出庭作证; 保证；证明；确定"} for every citation — they had spent a morning combing sources together. "I can [attest]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="attest · vt. 证明；证实；为…作证; 证明；作证"} to every figure we use," Mara would [utter]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="utter · vt. 以口发出声音; 说，讲; 彻底的；完全的；绝对的"} before each taping, a small ritual that kept both of them honest.

Midway through the episode, a viewer question arrived via live chat, riddled with what looked like a [cipher]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="cipher · n. 密码；暗号；零; 做算术；计算；使用密码; 做算术；计算；将…译成密码"} no one had asked to decode. The guest leaned forward to [beckon]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="beckon · vt. &amp; 示意, 召唤"} the camera closer, as though proximity might clarify meaning. He began to [babble]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="babble · vi. 喋喋不休；呀呀学语；作潺潺声; 含糊不清地说；泄露; 含糊不清的话；胡言乱语；潺潺声"} — not from nerves but from genuine excitement — layering clause upon clause before Mara gently raised a hand. She needed him to [affirm]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="affirm · vt. 断言；肯定; 断言；确认"} the single core point before the audience lost the thread. He [assented]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="assent · vi. 赞成；同意; 赞成；同意"} without bruising, and the two [concurred]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="concur · vi. 一致；同意；互助"} on a formulation that was honest and plain. To [assure]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="assure · vt. 保证；担保；使确信；弄清楚"} listeners that no nuance had been lost, Mara [alluded]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="allude · vi. 提及, 暗指"} briefly to the fuller argument and promised a link in the show notes — a quiet [tacit]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="tacit · adj. 缄默的,不说话的; 暗示的,不言而喻的; 不明言的,默许的; 由法律的效力而产生的,法定的"} agreement between host and guest that the detail mattered even if air-time did not allow it.

After the taping, the sound editor flagged a segment where a troll in the live chat had sent a [spoof]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="spoof · n. 滑稽模仿; 玩笑，讽刺性文章; 滑稽地模仿; 发送电邮；发送仿真电邮；电邮欺骗; 哄骗；捉弄"} account comment — little more than a malicious [tilde]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="tilde · n. 波浪字符；加在西班牙语n字上的发音符号"} decorating a fake handle — attempting to [accost]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="accost · vt. 勾引；引诱；对…说话；搭讪"} the guest with a distorted quote. The editor had already blocked the account. A researcher drafted a short thread to [deride]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="deride · vt. 嘲笑；嘲弄"} the misquote publicly, but the guest shook his head: better to [confer]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="confer · vt. 授予；给予; 协商"} with the legal team before publishing anything, and better still to let the [beacon]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="beacon · n. 灯塔，信号浮标；烽火；指路明灯; 照亮，指引; 像灯塔般照耀"} of an accurate transcript speak for itself rather than [bicker]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="bicker · vi. 闪动；斗嘴；潺潺而流; 吵嘴；口角；潺潺声"} with bad-faith actors. He had been [berated]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="berate · vt. 严责；申斥"} once, years ago, by an editor who said arguing with trolls was the fastest way to make a [cliche]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="cliche · n. 陈词滥调；铅版；陈腐思想; 陈腐的"} of yourself. He'd never forgotten it. The show would [troll]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="troll · vt. 轮唱，使转动；放声高唱；拖饵钓鱼; 参加轮唱；宏亮地唱；拖饵钓鱼; 轮唱；钓鱼"} no one back; it would simply keep doing the work.

### When Words Refuse to Stay Still

A retired diplomat once sat down to [peruse]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="peruse · vt. 详细考察；精读"} the [scroll]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="scroll · n. 纸卷, 卷轴; 涡卷形, 卷形花纹; 从上到下移动, 卷页; 卷起; 将文字显示于屏幕"} of handwritten dispatches she had kept since her first posting abroad. Fifty years of foreign service, and yet the act of reading her own sentences still felt like meeting a stranger. She had spent decades trying to [impart]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="impart · vt. 给予, 传授; 告知, 透露"} something true across every border — not merely facts, but feeling. In her early years she had relied on a [primer]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="primer · n. 初级读本；识字课本；原始物"} of polite formulas, the kind every junior attaché was handed, full of [jargon]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="jargon · n. 行话，术语；黄锆石"} that was meant to smooth negotiations but mostly produced a kind of [pidgin]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="pidgin · n. 洋泾滨语；混杂语言；事务"} diplomacy: fluent on the surface, hollow underneath.

She remembered the interpreter who could [elicit]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="elicit · vt. 引出, 探出"} a confession from a stone — a quiet man whose every [remark]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="remark · n. 话语，评论; 注意；看；观察; &amp; 谈论，评论; 注意到…"} seemed to [evince]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="evince · vt. 表明，表示；引起"} both patience and precision. He never needed to [holler]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="holler · vi. 发牢骚；叫喊；抱怨; 大声叫喊; 叫喊"} or [shriek]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="shriek · vt. &amp; 尖叫; 尖叫声"} to be heard. He never let [rumors]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="rumors · n. 谣传，流言; 谣传"} rattle his composure, even when the room filled with the [hoopla]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="hoopla · n. 投环套物游戏；喧闹"} of competing delegations. When a junior colleague tried to [palter]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="palter · vi. 含糊其词；马虎处理；敷衍了事；讨价还价"} over the wording of a joint statement, the interpreter simply waited, then offered one clean sentence that made all the [ironic]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="ironic · adj. 讽刺的；反话的"} hedging unnecessary. Colleagues who tried to [retort]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="retort · vt. 反驳; 反驳, 回嘴; 反驳的回答"} or [refute]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="refute · vt. 驳斥, 驳倒"} his readings usually found themselves outflanked by their own words.

The ambassador herself had been less measured. ### The Making of a Message

A young [columnist]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="columnist · n. 专栏作家"} sat at her desk, staring at a [facsimile]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="facsimile · n. 副本;传真"} of an ancient [cuneiform]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="cuneiform · adj. 楔形的,楔状骨的,楔形文字的; 楔形文字,楔状骨"} tablet her professor had once sent her — a reminder that humanity's impulse to communicate stretches back to the first scratched symbols. She had interviewed a veteran [publicist]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="publicist · n. 宣传人员;宣传代理人; 政论家;时事评论员"} that morning, a man famous for his skill at generating [publicity]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="publicity · n. 公众的注意, 众所周知; 宣传, 宣扬"} for clients teetering on the edge of scandal. He answered her questions [brusquely]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="brusquely · adv. 唐突地,粗率地"}, barely pausing between [assertion]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="assertion · n. 主张，维护；坚持; 强硬陈词；断言"} and counter-claim. When she asked whether he thought of himself as a mere [apologist]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="apologist · n. 辩解者；辩护士; 护教论者"} for bad behaviour, he cut her off: he was a [proponent]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="proponent · n. 支持者,拥护者"} of narrative, he said, not a spin doctor. His publicist's instinct was to [propagate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="propagate · vt. &amp; 繁衍，增殖; 传播；宣传，普及"} a preferred story before a rival version could take root, to [inculcate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="inculcate · vt. 极力主张, 反复灌输"} that story in every outlet willing to run it, and to [importune]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="importune · vt. 纠缠,向不断要求; 拉"} every editor who hesitated.

Back at her desk she reached for a grammar handbook and looked up how an [adjective]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="adjective · n."} could quietly tilt a sentence — the way a single modifier could carry more freight than a paragraph of plain statement. She noticed how she herself had started to [enunciate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="enunciate · vt. 发音; 确切地说明"} her own views more carefully lately, aware that words, once on record, get [hand down]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="hand down 宣布；把…传下去"} to audiences she would never meet. The piece would carry her [eponymous]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="eponymous · adj. 同名的，与作品同名的"} byline, though she had once written under a [pseudonym]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="pseudonym · n. 假名；笔名"} to protect a source. She used an [ampersand]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="ampersand · n. &amp;的记号名称"} to join two clauses in the headline — a small typographic choice — and watched the character count tick up. Outside, a pack of [Paparazzi]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Paparazzi )〈意〉无固定职业的摄影师"} clustered below a hotel entrance, cameras ready; their subjects existed, [literally]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="literally · adv. 逐字地；照字面地; 确实地，真正地"}, only as long as the lens agreed to find them. The [purported]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="purported · adj. 传说的,谣传的"} star never emerged, but the photographers stayed, because the possibility of a picture is itself a kind of [adulation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="adulation · n. 谄媚；奉承"}, a silent insistence that someone is worth watching. ### The Language of a Long Day

At the editorial board's year-end [symposium]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="symposium · n. 讨论会, 专题报告"}, a junior editor rose to [reiterate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="reiterate · vt. 反复地说,重申; 反复地说,重申; 反复说的,重申的"} the team's standing rule: every [manuscript]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="manuscript · n. 手稿, 原稿, 底稿; 手写本"} submitted must include proper [annotation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="annotation · n. 注解,注释"} and any supporting [appendices]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="appendices 附录,附属品,阑尾"} before it enters review. She spoke [explicitly]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="explicitly · adv. 明白地,明确地"}, determined not to let ambiguity breed another round of corrections.

[By the way]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="by the way 在途中；顺便说说，顺便问一下"}, she added, the style guide had been updated — writers should no longer rely on [colloquial]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="colloquial · adj. 口语的, 会话的"} phrasing when precision mattered, nor should they [exaggerate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="exaggerate · vt. &amp; 扩大, 增加; 夸大, 夸张"} a finding simply to [accentuate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="accentuate · vt. 使突出；强调; 重读，以重音读出; 加重音符号于; 使恶化，使严重"} its impact. Her tone was firm but never [accusatory]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="accusatory · adj. 非难的,控诉的,指责的"}; she had no wish to seem [derogatory]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="derogatory · adj. 不敬的"} toward the freelancers who had missed the mark. Still, she did not [repudiate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="repudiate · vt. 拒绝接受, 否认, 否定; 拒绝偿付"} the criticism either. She read aloud a [memorandum]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="memorandum · n. 记录; 非正式商业书信,便函"} a senior editor had drafted — a [cautionary]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="cautionary · adj. 提醒注意的, 告诫的"} note about a recent piece whose [discursive]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="discursive · adj. 散漫的；离题的；东拉西扯的；无层次的"} structure had buried its argument under [ironically]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="ironically · adv. 嘲讽地, 挖苦地; 具有讽刺意味地"} verbose paragraphs.

A [dissenting]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="dissenting · adj. 不同意的"} voice came from the back: a veteran writer who served as the magazine's unofficial [mouthpiece]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="mouthpiece · n. 烟斗的嘴,乐器的吹口; 话筒; 喉舌,代言人,传声筒"} for contributors. He argued, without trying to [contradict]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="contradict · vt. &amp; 反驳, 否认…的真实性; 与…发生矛盾, 与…抵触"} the rule itself, that the new guidelines punished voice. One editor issued what amounted to a quiet [reprimand]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="reprimand · n. 训斥, 惩戒; 申斥, 惩戒, 谴责"}, noting that a [compliment]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="compliment · n. 赞美，恭维; 向…送礼以表示敬意; 表扬；恭维"} for strong prose did not excuse weak sourcing. Someone consulting a [thesaurus]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="thesaurus · n. 同义词词典，类属词典; 百科全书；汇编，文选; 宝库，仓库"} for every [vocabular]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="vocabular · adj. 词汇的"} choice, another quipped, was not the same as thinking clearly. The [persuasion]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="persuasion · n. 劝说; 说服; 信仰"} that finally settled the room came from the editor-in-chief, who held up a draft page where a single [participle]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="participle · n. 分词"} had been misused across four [inscribing]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="inscribing · n. 登记, 买或卖股票, 注册"} passes without anyone catching it. What mattered was that from this meeting forward, every editorial decision be made — and recorded — without [accusatory]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="accusatory · adj. 非难的,控诉的,指责的"} hedging, without vague [imputation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="imputation · n. 归罪;负责; 诋毁；非难;污名"}, and without the kind of language that a reader could only parse as a coded [reprimand]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="reprimand · n. 训斥, 惩戒; 申斥, 惩戒, 谴责"} buried in [compliment]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="compliment · n. 赞美，恭维; 向…送礼以表示敬意; 表扬；恭维"}.

### When Words Fail — and When They Don't

A doctoral candidate sat in the archive, rifling through footnotes for her [dissertation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="dissertation · n. 专题论文, 学位论文"}. She had spent months building her [bibliography]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="bibliography · n. 书目; 书志学, 文献学"}, cross-checking every source against the [encyclopedia]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="encyclopedia · n. 百科全书; 专科全书"} of linguistics her advisor kept on the shared shelf. The topic was deceptively narrow: how speakers [communicate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="communicate · vt. &amp; 传达；表达; 通讯；交际，交流; 相连；相通"} not just meaning but mood — how the same sentence, read [figuratively]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="figuratively · adv. 比喻地;象征性地"}, carries connotations no [sentential]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="sentential · adj. 句子的,判决的,判决上的"} analysis alone can capture.

Her argument was [persuasive]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="persuasive · adj. 能说服的;善于游说的"} on the surface, but her committee had flagged a problem. One paragraph leaned so heavily on a famous theorist's phrasing that it edged toward [plagiarism]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="plagiarism · n. 剽窃,抄袭; 剽窃物,抄袭物"}; she had, in effect, begun to [plagiarize]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="plagiarize · vt. 剽窃,抄袭"} without realizing it, lifting the structure while swapping synonyms. She rewrote the section, this time letting the [vernacular]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="vernacular · n. 本国语，本地话，方言; 行话; 白话；白话文; 动植物的俗名; 本国语的；白话的；方言的; 本国的；…"} of her own field carry the weight — the informal, living [descriptive]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="descriptive · adj. 说明的;解释的; 描写的"} language that practitioners actually use, not the polished register of translated theory. She worked to make every claim [unequivocal]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="unequivocal · adj. 只有一种含意的;清楚明白的; 只有一种含意地;清楚明白地"}, stripping out the [exaggerated]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="exaggerated · adj. 夸大的,言过其实的,夸张的"} hedges that had crept in during tired late-night drafts. Where she had inserted a long [parenthesis]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="parenthesis · n. 插入语,插入成分; 圆括号; 间歇,插曲"} about historical context, she cut it to a single clause so the logic stayed tight and the [conjunction]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="conjunction · n. 连词; 结合; 联合"} between evidence and conclusion was clear.

The real trouble came during the defense. The [prolocutor]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="prolocutor · n. 主席; 发言人"} — a senior professor who chaired proceedings — pressed her on a slide. Had she used a [red herring]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="red herring 熏青鱼；转移注意力的话题；与事实不相干的论点"} to sidestep a methodological flaw? She paused. The question carried [rhetorical]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="rhetorical · adj. 修辞的, 用来产生修辞效果的; 言辞的，口头的"} force designed to unsettle her. She recognized the [propaganda]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="propaganda · n. 宣传, 宣传运动"} move: frame the weakness as disqualifying before she could explain it. She refused to be distracted. Instead, she chose to [underscore]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="underscore · vt. 划线于…下,强调; 底线"} the one finding that mattered, [disseminate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="disseminate · vt. 散布, 传播"} its implications clearly across three fields, and [promulgate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="promulgate · vt. 宣扬；传播; 公布，颁布; 颁布者，公布者"} a [proverbial]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="proverbial · adj. 谚语的；谚语式的；众所周知的"} caution the committee itself had ignored: extraordinary claims need extraordinary evidence. Her phrasing was careful — no [misstatement]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="misstatement · n. 误述,虚伪陈述"}, no [misinterpret]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="misinterpret · vt. 误解；曲解; 误解；曲解"}-able slide, no [incoherence]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="incoherence · n. 不连贯，无条理"} between data and conclusion. The [connotation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="connotation · n. 内涵；含蓄；暗示，隐含意义；储蓄的东西"} of every term had been weighed. When one examiner muttered that a rival paper was [full of crap]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="full of crap"}, the prolocutor said simply: [knock it off]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="knock it off"}. Later, reading the [transcript]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="transcript · n. 抄本; 誊本; 打字本; 副本; 学生成绩报告单"} of the session, she noticed how much of academic discourse depended on knowing when precision served truth and when it merely performed it.

### When the Microphone Is Hot

The [valedictorian]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="valedictorian · n. 致告别辞者,告别演说者"} stepped up to the podium, her notes loaded into the [teleprompter]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="teleprompter · n. 讲词提示机"}, and cleared her throat. She had spent weeks polishing every line, swapping out [polysyllabic]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="polysyllabic · adj. 多音节的"} tangents for plain, punchy sentences, because — as her coach liked to say — it goes [without further ado]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Without further ado."} that clarity beats cleverness in a packed auditorium. A foreign [correspondent]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="correspondent · n. 通讯员, 记者; 通信者"} seated in the front row scribbled away, already framing her [complimentary]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="complimentary · adj. 表示敬意的，赞美的，恭维的; 赠送的; 崇敬地,赞美地,赞许地"} lead paragraph.

Backstage, the student emcee was practicing a [tongue twister]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="tongue twister 绕口令"} to warm up, pausing every few lines to let his [witty wordplay]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="witty wordplay"} land before moving on. The event program itself had required careful [disambiguation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="disambiguation · n. 解疑,消除模棱两可情况"} — "address" meaning speech, not location — because the original draft had been nearly [unintelligible]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="unintelligible · adj. 不可能理解的; 难懂的"} to the volunteer translators working in three languages. English served as the de-facto [lingua franca]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="lingua franca 通用语；共通语；混合语"} of the conference, bridging delegates who, [metaphorically]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="metaphorically · adv. 比喻地,隐喻地"} speaking, were sailing in very different waters. The simultaneous [interpretation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="interpretation · n. 解释，说明；诠释; 表演；演奏"} booth hummed quietly above them all.

When the ceremony finally began, the emcee warned the audience not to [blurt stuff out]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="blurt stuff out"} during the citation readings. Applause, he reminded them, was the proper [acknowledgement]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="acknowledgement · n. 答谢的表示; 确认收到的信等; 致谢, 鸣谢"} — a small but meaningful signal in a room where every word was being weighed. It goes [without further ado]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Without further ado."}, he added with a grin, and the crowd laughed, understanding him completely.
